frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Four SPWs (two USB, two LSB): one FDM SPW with 1.875 GHz bandwidth and 7.82 MHz (~16.6 km/s) channel width; three TDM SPWs with 2.0 GHz bandwidth and 15.6 MHz resolution

evidence.quote: We used four spectral windows (SPWs), two of each were placed in the upper and the lower sideband, respectively.
One SPW was set in the Frequency-Division Mode (FDM) to detect the redshifted [C I ] (1–0) with a channel width of 7.82 MHz ( ∼ 16.6 km s − 1 ) covering 1.875 GHz bandwidth.
The remaining three SPWs were observed in the Time-Division Mode (TDM) with a 2.0-GHz bandwidth at the 15.6-MHz resolution to cover the dust continuum at 2 mm.

We revisit the cold gas contents of galaxies in a protocluster at z = 2.49 using the lowest neutral atomic carbon transition [C I ] 3P1 − 3P0 from Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array observations.

findings_qualitative.value: Five out of sixteen targeted protocluster HAEs are detected in [C I] (1-0) (HAE 3, 4, 8, 9, and 16), all of which were previously detected in CO (3-2) and CO (4-3).

evidence.quote: Five galaxies out of sixteen targeted galaxies are detected in the [C I ] line, and these are all previously detected in CO (3–2) and CO (4–3) and three in 1.1 mm dust continuum.

evidence.loc: 3.1. Detection of [C I ] and line properties compared to CO
evidence.quote: We detect the [C I ] line from five galaxies previously detected in CO (3–2) and CO (4–3) lines, i.e., HAE 3, 4, 8, 9 and 16.

findings_qualitative.value: The log L'_CO(4-3) - log L'_[CI](1-0) relation in the protocluster is super-linear, consistent with literature field galaxies, with a hint of a shallower slope and higher normalization that may indicate denser gas.

evidence.loc: 3.2. The L ′ [CI](1 − 0) – L ′ CO(J − J − 1) relation
evidence.quote: For log L ′ CO(4 − 3) − log L ′ [CI](1 − 0) relation, the slope is super-linear for the protocluster members, consistent with other best-fit using the literature values.

evidence.loc: 3.2. The L ′ [CI](1 − 0) – L ′ CO(J − J − 1) relation
evidence.quote: If we can apply a similar interpretation, a hint of a shallower slope (close to a linear relation) and a higher normalization factor in protocluster galaxies than other high- z main-sequence galaxies might hint at the existence of more denser gas in protocluster galaxies than high- z field main-sequence galaxies.

findings_qualitative.value: Molecular gas masses from [C I], CO (3-2), and 1.1 mm dust agree within ~0.3 dex using field main-sequence calibrations, though CO-based estimates are ~40% (0.14 dex) higher on average, suggesting alpha_CO * R_13 may need to be lowered for some galaxies (HAE 3, 10, 16).

evidence.loc: 3.3. Molecular gas mass from [C I ], CO and dust
evidence.quote: In summary, three gas tracers are broadly in good agreement for the inferred molecular masses within ≈ 0.3 dex, but CO-based gas measurements give ≈ 40% (0.14 dex) higher value than other gas tracers on average.
Overall, there is a hint that the assumed α CO × R 13 needs to be lowered for HAE 3, 10, and 16 (thus reducing the CObased gas mass), though it is not conclusive for the remaining galaxies.

findings_qualitative.value: The mean gas fraction of the protocluster galaxies for log(M_star/M_sun) = [10.6, 11.3] is comparable to field galaxies (~50%), while the gas depletion time scale decreases more rapidly with stellar mass than in field galaxies.

evidence.quote: We generally reconfirm our previous findings that the mean gas fraction is comparable to field galaxies for a stellar mass range of log M star /M ⊙ = [10.6 , 11.3] ( f gas = M gas / ( M gas + M star ) ≈ 50%)).
At least for these five [C I ] detected galaxies, the depletion time scale decreases more rapidly with stellar mass than field galaxies that might lead galaxies to quench earlier than field galaxies.

claims.hypothesis: Field main-sequence molecular gas mass calibrations for [C I] (1-0), CO (3-2), and dust continuum can be applied to z = 2.49 protocluster galaxies.
claims.experiment: Observed 16 protocluster HAEs in ALMA Band 4 for [C I] (1-0), reanalyzed archival CO (3-2), CO (4-3), and 1.1 mm dust continuum fluxes with a unified CASA imfit procedure, and compared derived molecular gas masses using standard field main-sequence conversion factors.
claims.result: Five galaxies are detected in [C I]; [C I]-based gas masses agree with dust-based masses within 0.16 dex (mean difference 0.02 dex) and are lower than or comparable to CO-based masses by up to -0.35 dex (mean deviation -0.14 dex).
claims.finding: [C I] is a reliable molecular gas tracer in protocluster galaxies using the field main-sequence calibration log(X_CI) = -4.8, though alpha_CO * R_13 may be overestimated by up to ~0.35-0.43 dex in three galaxies.

evidence.quote: Using the calibration adopted for field main-sequence galaxies, the [C I ] -based gas measurements are lower than or comparable to the CO-based gas measurements by -0.35 dex at the lowest with the mean deviation of -0.14 dex. The differences between [C I ] - and the dust- based measurements are relatively mild by up to 0.16 dex with the mean difference of 0.02 dex.

evidence.loc: 4.2. Gas depletion time scale compared to field galaxies
evidence.quote: In the previous section, we showed that the [C I ] line is a reliable gas tracer of protocluster galaxies. The same calibration of log( X CI ) = − 4.8 applied for the field main-sequence galaxies can be used for these galaxies.

claims.hypothesis: The L'_CO - L'_[CI](1-0) luminosity relations in z = 2.49 protocluster galaxies follow those of field galaxies.
claims.experiment: Performed orthogonal distance regression fits to log L'_CO(4-3) vs log L'_[CI](1-0) and log L'_CO(3-2) vs log L'_[CI](1-0) for six secure protocluster galaxies and compared with literature compilations.
claims.result: For CO (4-3), the protocluster slope is super-linear (a = 1.16 +/- 0.23, b = 10.46 +/- 0.08), consistent with literature fits; for CO (3-2), the variable-slope fit is sub-linear (a = 0.43 +/- 0.20) compared to DSFG-dominated literature (a = 1.32 +/- 0.10), over a narrow luminosity dynamic range.
claims.finding: The super-linear CO (4-3)-[C I] relation is consistent with field galaxies and may hint at denser gas in protocluster galaxies, while the current sample size and narrow dynamic range prevent a robust conclusion on systematic environmental differences.

evidence.loc: 3.2. The L ′ [CI](1 − 0) – L ′ CO(J − J − 1) relation
evidence.quote: For log L ′ CO(4 − 3) − log L ′ [CI](1 − 0) relation, the slope is super-linear for the protocluster members, consistent with other best-fit using the literature values.

evidence.quote: The current data set is not sufficient to robustly conclude because of the the low number statistics and unknown systematic biases for currently available data sets in different environments.

claims.hypothesis: Protocluster galaxies at z = 2.49 exhibit a steeper decline in gas depletion time scale with stellar mass than field main-sequence galaxies.
claims.experiment: Calculated [C I]-based gas depletion time scales normalized by three field scaling relations (Scoville et al. 2017; Tacconi et al. 2018; Liu et al. 2019) as a function of stellar mass and tested correlations with Spearman's rank coefficient.
claims.result: Found negative Spearman correlation coefficients of -0.81 (p = 0.008), -0.68 (p = 0.04), and -0.53 (p = 0.14) including upper limits (and -0.9, p = 0.04 for secure detections), whereas z ~ 1 field control samples show weaker correlations (-0.35 to +0.23).
claims.finding: The gas depletion time scale decreases more rapidly with stellar mass in the protocluster than in the field, reconfirming earlier CO/dust results and suggesting faster gas consumption or removal in massive protocluster galaxies.

evidence.quote: However, at least for these secure five detections, the depletion time scale decreases more rapidly with stellar mass than field galaxies that might be related to earlier quenching in dense environments.

evidence.loc: 4.2. Gas depletion time scale compared to field galaxies
evidence.quote: We find negative Spearman coefficient values ( p -value) of -0.81 (0.008, Scoville et al. 2017), -0.68 (0.04, Tacconi et al. 2018), -0.53 (0.14, Liu et al. 2019), when the 3 σ upper limits are all taken into account. We also note that the correlation coefficient is -0.9 with p-value of 0.04 if only the secure detections are considered.

why_this_data.value: [C I] (1-0) is an independent, optically thin molecular gas tracer less sensitive to excitation temperature and robust against low metallicity and cosmic rays, allowing an independent test of CO and dust gas mass calibrations in a protocluster.

evidence.quote: Such a test is necessary by using an independent method, whether the calibration of field galaxies can be applied in the same manner. Fine structure lines of atomic carbon [C I ] is an alternative tracer of the molecular gas.

The lowest transition of [C I ] 3P1 − 3P0 (hereafter written simply as the [C I ] (1–0) transition) is optically thin in most cases, less sensitive to excitation temperature compared to [C I ] 3P2 − 3P1 (hereafter [C I ] (2–1)) when converting to a mass (Weiß et al. 2005).

why_this_method.value: Subtracted continuum on 10'' x 10'' subcubes to improve subtraction for galaxies far from the phase center; reanalyzed CO (3-2), CO (4-3), and dust with the same imfit and aperture procedure to eliminate systematic errors from differing flux measurement methods.

evidence.quote: We subtracted the continuum emission on the image domain using imcontsub (fitorder = 0) after we made smaller data cubes (10 ′′ × 10 ′′ ) centered on the target HAEs. This is to get improved results of continuum subtraction for galaxies not close to the phase center.

evidence.loc: 2.3. Reanalysis of previous CO and dust measurements
evidence.quote: We reanalyzed the CO (3–2), CO (4–3), and dust data for unified analyses to reduce the systematic errors coming from different flux measurement methods.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using a fixed 1''.0 circular aperture for all galaxies instead of S/N-optimized apertures (0''.7 for HAE 4); found to give consistent flux estimates.

evidence.loc: 2.3. Reanalysis of previous CO and dust measurements

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using 50 km s^-1 vs 80 km s^-1 velocity binning for low S/N galaxies (HAE 3 and HAE 4); confirmed no change in line widths and fluxes within uncertainties.

evidence.quote: For low S/N galaxies (HAE 4 and HAE 3), we also checked whether different velocity binnings (50 km s − 1 versus 80 km s − 1 ) change our results. We confirmed that the results did not change in terms of the line widths and fluxes within uncertainties between two different velocity binnings.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Metallicity-dependent alpha_CO correction; rejected because for log(M_star/M_sun) > 10.5 it only increases gas estimates by up to 0.07 dex for the lowest mass galaxies.

evidence.loc: 3.3. Molecular gas mass from [C I ], CO and dust
evidence.quote: Here, we don’t correct for the metallicity-dependence of the α CO conversion factor. For the underlying stellar mass range that we observe (log ( M star /M ⊙ ) > 10.5), the metallicity-dependent α CO factor only increases the gas estimate the up to 0.07 dex for the lowest mass galaxies (HAE 16 and HAE 10) and does not affect higher mass regime.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Recalibrating both X_CI (lowered by 0.35 dex) and dust temperature (T_d < 20 K) to match the CO-based gas mass in HAE 10; rejected as less likely than lowering alpha_CO * R_13.

evidence.loc: C. GAS MASS CROSS CALIBRATION OF INDIVIDUAL GALAXIES
evidence.quote: To be consistent, α CO × R 13 should be lowered by a factor of ≈ 2.7, otherwise, both the X CI and dust temperature need to be recalibrated. The latter case is less likely, because X CI needs to be lowered by 0.35 dex, and the dust temperature should be lower than 20 K unless the difference is due to a higher gas-to-dust ratio.

limitations_admitted.value: Potential selection biases from the flux-limited H alpha narrow-band selection and the specific halo properties of a single protocluster.

evidence.quote: With limited number of galaxies detected in [C I ] (also CO and dust), it is difficult to verify whether there is any selection bias delivering such mass dependency. Such bias could originate not only from the flux-limited galaxy selection (H α ) but also from the halo property (mass, evolutionary stage) of the protocluster.

referee_caveats_inferred: Single-line CO (4-3) detections (HAE 1, 2, 7, 12, 23) have lower significance upon reanalysis and are excluded from the main line ratio fits.
Literature CO (3-2) vs [C I] comparison sample is heavily biased toward high-z DSFGs with only one main-sequence galaxy.
Spatial and velocity offsets between [C I], CO (3-2), and CO (4-3) in merging/extended sources (HAE 3, 4, 9) introduce aperture and velocity-range sensitivity in flux ratios.
